comments.content: [medium] Fold `READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY` into `read_flags` doesn't feel right conceptually: primary/replica is persistent client state, while the bits in this mask are transient per-read flags that vary from one operation to the next. Bundling them into the same bitmask conflates state that gets set once with flags tied to individual requests.

[medium] Possible buffer overflow here: if `bufpos < c->ref_block_pos`, the subtraction underflows because `size_t` is unsigned, yielding an enormous value that gets handed to `connWrite`. Consider guarding with `if (bufpos <= c->ref_block_pos) return;` ahead of the `connWrite` call.
[low] Please ensure that `READ_FLAGS_PRIMARY` is not evaluated before the required state has been initialized.
